Sean Durzi is on injured reserve and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Braden Schneider has taken his spot beside Marcus Pettersson. That pair has had 60% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 45:51 together, up from 45% with Durzi.

VAN.head: The Canucks have their work cut out
VAN.body: Even though Vancouver has home-ice advantage, the Rangers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks can still win it if they get good looks, but a lot has to go their way.

NYR.head: The Rangers should be favored
NYR.body: Even though Vancouver has home-ice advantage, the Rangers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks’ best way in is getting good looks.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Rangers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-2 in New York on Oct 11. The Canucks are on a four-game losing streak, while the Rangers have won two in a row. Going in, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

The Rangers’ record (.559) is about what their chances are worth. The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.194) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .323, mostly because they’re 2-5 in one-goal games.

The Rangers lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest), forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Canucks pick their shots (lowest) and have had shaky goaltending (32nd). They also have a leaky penalty kill (32nd), so the Rangers’ power play (8th) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded. Vancouver has allowed 4.61 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Adam Fox (2 G / 19 A / 21 P in 17 GP) leads the Rangers in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 17 GP) has a team-high nine goals. For the Canucks, Elias Pettersson (#40) (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 18 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Brock Boeser (6 G / 9 A / 15 P in 18 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Dylan Garand (6-6-1 / .906 SV% in 11 GS) will likely start for the Rangers, and Leevi Meriläinen (2-6-1 / .889 SV% in 10 GS) for Vancouver.
At home, Manny Malhotra likes to send Cotter, Sasson and Gallagher out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Chmelař, Laba and Rempe.

The Canucks are newly without Filip Chytil and Tom Willander, and have had to make do without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.
Liam Öhgren has six goals on chances worth about 2.9 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Pavel Dorofeyev has five goals on chances worth about 7.2 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
